:::{#exm-cond-mixed}

#### Conditional expectation, one discrete variable and one continuous variable

**$X$ discrete, $Y$ continuous.**
The `plasma` dataset in the `dobson` package
(@dobson4e, Table 6.25)
records plasma inorganic phosphate levels (mg/dL)
one hour after a glucose tolerance test,
for hyperinsulinemic obese (`H-O`) and control (`C`) participants.
Let $X$ be group and $Y$ be phosphate level.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
plasma_summary <-
  dobson::plasma |>
  dplyr::filter(Group %in% c("H-O", "C")) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    .by = Group,
    n = dplyr::n(),
    mean = mean(phosphate),
    sd = sd(phosphate)
  )
group_stat <- function(group, stat) {
  plasma_summary[[stat]][plasma_summary[["Group"]] == group]
}
n_ho <- group_stat("H-O", "n")
n_c <- group_stat("C", "n")
mean_ho <- group_stat("H-O", "mean")
sd_ho <- group_stat("H-O", "sd")
mean_c <- group_stat("C", "mean")
sd_c <- group_stat("C", "sd")
pander::pander(plasma_summary)
```

Modeling phosphate as approximately normal within each group,
with parameters set equal to each group's sample mean and SD,
and $\P(X = \text{H-O}) = `r n_ho`/`r n_ho + n_c`$:

$$Y \mid X = \text{H-O} \sim \ndist{`r round(mean_ho, 2)`,\, `r round(sd_ho, 2)`^2}$$
$$Y \mid X = \text{C} \sim \ndist{`r round(mean_c, 2)`,\, `r round(sd_c, 2)`^2}$$

By @def-cond-mixed, since the mean of a normal distribution
is its location parameter:

$$\E{Y \mid X = \text{H-O}} = `r round(mean_ho, 2)` \text{ mg/dL}, \qquad
  \E{Y \mid X = \text{C}} = `r round(mean_c, 2)` \text{ mg/dL}$$

**$X$ continuous, $Y$ discrete.**
The `senility` dataset in the `dobson` package
(@dobson4e, Table 7.8)
records, for 54 elderly people,
a WAIS (Wechsler Adult Intelligence Scale) score
and whether symptoms of senility were present.
Let $X$ be WAIS score and $Y$ indicate senility symptoms.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
senility_fit <- glm(s ~ x, data = dobson::senility, family = binomial)
b0 <- coef(senility_fit)[["(Intercept)"]]
b1 <- coef(senility_fit)[["x"]]
pander::pander(coef(senility_fit))
```

Modeling $\P(Y = 1 \mid X = x)$ with the fitted logistic regression:

$$\logit \P(Y = 1 \mid X = x) = `r sprintf("%.4f", b0)` - `r sprintf("%.4f", abs(b1))`\, x$$

By @def-cond-mixed, since $Y \mid X=x$ is Bernoulli:

$$
\ba
\E{Y \mid X = x} &= 0 \cd \P(Y=0 \mid X=x) + 1 \cd \P(Y=1 \mid X=x)
&& \text{(definition of conditional expectation, mixed case)}
\\&= \P(Y=1 \mid X=x)
&& \text{(simplify)}
\\&= \frac{1}{1 + \e{-(`r sprintf("%.4f", b0)` - `r sprintf("%.4f", abs(b1))`\, x)}}
&& \text{(invert the logit)}
\ea
$$

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
senility_p10 <- predict(
  senility_fit,
  newdata = tibble::tibble(x = 10),
  type = "response"
)
senility_p15 <- predict(
  senility_fit,
  newdata = tibble::tibble(x = 15),
  type = "response"
)
```

At $x = 10$: $\E{Y \mid X=10} = `r round(senility_p10, 2)`$.
At $x = 15$: $\E{Y \mid X=15} = `r round(senility_p15, 2)`$ ---
a lower WAIS score is associated with higher predicted probability
of senility symptoms.

:::
